plan: In a second-price sealed-bid auction, bidding your true value is a dominant strategy regardless of the number of competitors. This is because you pay the second-highest bid if you win, not your own bid, so there's no incentive to shade your bid. Bidding above value risks overpaying; bidding below value risks losing profitable auctions. With no prior round history to adjust for, I will bid my true value of $20.

This is a second-price auction, where bidding your true value is the dominant strategy regardless of what others do. If I bid my true value of $29, I win whenever my value exceeds the second-highest bid, and I pay only that second-highest bid - ensuring I never overpay and always capture positive surplus when I win. Bidding higher risks negative profit; bidding lower risks losing profitable opportunities. Therefore, I will bid exactly my value.

In a second-price auction, bidding your true value is a dominant strategy regardless of other bidders' behavior. This is because you pay the second-highest bid, not your own bid, so overbidding risks paying more than the item's worth, while underbidding risks losing profitable wins. With a private value of $45, the optimal strategy is to bid exactly $45, ensuring I win whenever profitable and pay only the second-highest bid.
